verses.text: Jotham was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Jerushah the daughter of Zadok.
He did that which was right in Yahweh’s eyes, according to all that his father Uzziah had done. However he didn’t enter into Yahweh’s temple. The people still acted corruptly.
He built the upper gate of Yahweh’s house, and he built much on the wall of Ophel.
Moreover he built cities in the hill country of Judah, and in the forests he built fortresses and towers.

He also fought with the king of the children of Ammon, and prevailed against them. The children of Ammon gave him the same year one hundred talents  of silver, ten thousand cors  of wheat, and ten thousand cors of barley.  The children of Ammon also gave that much to him in the second year, and in the third.
So Jotham became mighty, because he ordered his ways before Yahweh his God.
Now the rest of the acts of Jotham, and all his wars, and his ways, behold, they are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.
He was five and twenty years old when he began to reign, and reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem.
Jotham slept with his fathers, and they buried him in David’s city; and Ahaz his son reigned in his place.

footnotes.content: Jotham began young—only twenty-five—with a long road ahead. His mother bore the name Jerushah, 'possessing' or 'possession of the Lord.' How often the Lord plants faithfulness in a young heart through faithful parents, though the son must still choose the narrow way himself.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Here is a quiet boundary: Jotham walked in his father's footsteps—doing right in the Lord's eyes—yet he kept a respectful distance from the temple itself. Sometimes a faithful heart honors what is sacred by approaching it with fear, not presumption. The people's corruption around him only sharpens his own choice to remain upright.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He built the upper gate—a real threshold—and strengthened the wall of Ophel, the fortress ridge of Jerusalem. A king who builds what endures shapes not just stone but the people's sense of security. Notice: he strengthened a wall, not torn one down. That is the work of a steady hand.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: In Judah's hill country and forests, he raised fortresses and towers. A careful king thinks ahead, building where an enemy might come. His work was not splashy or central, but strategic—the sort of quiet stewardship that protects an entire people from harm.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Ammonites, who had troubled Judah, now paid tribute year after year—not because Jotham was harsh, but because he prevailed. Here the Lord honors a king's courage with prosperity and honor. Silver, wheat, barley—the gifts of a defeated enemy became sustenance for a strengthened kingdom. Even ancient readers would see: faithfulness brings overflow.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "He became mighty because he ordered his ways before Yahweh his God." This is the secret the world never learns: power flows from obedience, not from grasping it. Jotham did not seize greatness—he arranged his life toward the Lord, and strength followed as naturally as a shadow follows the sun.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: His deeds were written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah—the historical record of his generation. We are told plainly: this king's wars and ways were known and preserved. Yet most of what made Jotham great—his daily choices, his ordering of himself before God—these lay beneath the surface, seen only by those near him and by the Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Verse 8 mirrors verse 1, reminding us of his reign's span: sixteen years of steadiness. When a life is lived well, the Lord allows us to see the arc of it—not all at once, but long enough to recognize that a pattern of faithfulness compounds into a kingdom strengthened.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jotham slept with his fathers, buried in David's city where kings rest. The ancient reader understood: a faithful king joins the line of David. Today we hear an echo—those who order their ways toward the Lord join a communion of saints across the ages, a people whose rest is secure in the Lord's care. As of 2026-10, that continuity still holds: the faithful sleep knowing they belong to something that outlasts them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
